Variants.Content: Tolos is located in Slaver's Bay and the coast of Gith on the south coast of Essos, politically within the Giskali cities and their hinterland. It is a town, a center where surrounding populations, markets, roads and local power converge. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.
Entry Tolos Local families also relied on irrigation fields, brick kilns, harbors, caravans, and shipping along Slaver's Bay; if any road, well, or wharf failed, the cost would fall first on them.

Entry Tolos They will also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the Guise Coast; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Tolos If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Stone and wood will decay, but Troos still relies on craftsmen to take care of ship repair wood, canvas, salt, fish catch, and stones to resist the sea wind, and relies on priests to preserve the hierarchical order of the gods of Ghis, the step pyramid, and the ancient city-state. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Tolos They care about irrigation lands, brick kilns, ports, caravans, and shipping along Slaver's Bay. They also look at whether seeds are left after grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
